content:
The [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Find broken links on any page — every link checked, status reported. Enter your page URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find the broken links on a web page: enter a URL, and the tool fetches the page, collects every link on it (up to 50 per run), and checks each one, reporting the HTTP status — 200 for working, 404 for not found, and so on. Broken links hurt visitors and search engines alike: a page full of dead links looks unmaintained and wastes crawl budget. The checks run from this site's server with the same safety limits as the other audit tools, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Broken Link Checker

Start by typing or pasting your page URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the full URL of the page to check, starting with https://.
2. Run the check — up to 50 links are tested, a few seconds in total.
3. Fix or remove any link that does not return a working status.

## How it works

The [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Checking a page with 12 links reports 11 working (200) and 1 broken (404) — the broken one is listed with its address so you can fix or remove it. Try the same figures in the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What counts as broken

Any link that does not return a successful status: 404 (not found) is the usual one, but 500 errors, timeouts and connection failures count too. Redirects (301/302) are followed and reported with their final status, so a link that redirects to a working page is not flagged. Links starting with # (same-page anchors), mailto: and tel: are skipped — they are not web pages.

## Why broken links matter

A visitor who clicks a dead link hits an error page and often leaves. Search engines treat a page full of dead links as unmaintained, and every crawl of a dead link is crawl budget spent on nothing. Link rot is constant — sites move, rename and delete pages — so checking your important pages every few months is worth the few minutes it takes.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check your most-linked pages first — home, top posts, resource pages.
- A link that redirects to a working page is fine; one that redirects to an error is not.
- Re-check after fixing — a mistyped replacement link is easy to miss.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a broken link?

A link that leads nowhere — usually a 404 (page not found), a server error, or a connection failure. This tool checks every link on a page and reports the status of each one. Try it with your own numbers in the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many links does it check?

Up to 50 links per run. If a page has more, the first 50 are checked and the tool says how many were found in total. Try it with your own numbers in the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Are redirects counted as broken?

No. Redirects are followed to their final destination and reported with that page's status — only links that end in an error count as broken. Try it with your own numbers in the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I check a whole website?

This tool checks one page at a time. For a whole site, run it on your most important pages, or use a desktop crawler for a full sweep. Try it with your own numbers in the [Broken Link Checker](/broken-link-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
